questions.q: Which S3 event type covers any way an object gets created (PUT, POST, COPY, or multipart completion)?
options: s3:ObjectCreated:*
s3:ObjectRemoved:*
s3:ObjectRestore:*
s3:BucketCreated:*
questions.explain: s3:ObjectCreated:* fires for any object-creation action, whether it's a simple PUT, a POST, a COPY, or a completed multipart upload.

questions.q: What are the three destinations S3 event notifications can route directly to?
options: SNS, SQS, and Lambda
Glue, Athena, and Redshift
IAM, CloudTrail, and CloudWatch
EC2, ECS, and Fargate only
questions.explain: S3 event notifications route to SNS (fan-out), SQS (durable queue), or Lambda (direct invoke) — EventBridge is also available for more flexible rule-based routing.

questions.q: Why would you choose SNS over Lambda as an S3 event destination?
options: When more than one downstream system needs to react to the same event (fan-out)
SNS is required for any event with a prefix filter
SNS processes events faster than Lambda in all cases
Lambda cannot be triggered by S3 events at all
questions.explain: SNS is built for fan-out — publishing one event to multiple subscribers at once — which Lambda alone (a single direct invoke) doesn't provide.

questions.q: In the raw-zone ETL trigger pattern described in this lesson, what starts the Glue job?
options: An S3 ObjectCreated event scoped to a prefix, triggering a Lambda function that calls glue:StartJobRun
A CloudWatch alarm checking CPU usage
A manual click in the AWS console every time a file lands
An hourly scheduled job that polls the bucket for new files
questions.explain: The event-driven pattern uses an ObjectCreated notification (scoped by prefix/suffix) to invoke Lambda, which can call glue:StartJobRun to kick off the ETL job — no polling involved.

questions.q: Why is an event-driven trigger a better fit than a scheduled polling job for unpredictable file arrival times?
options: The pipeline only runs, and only costs anything, when data actually arrives — instead of checking on a timer regardless of whether new data exists
Scheduled jobs are not supported by AWS at all
Event-driven triggers are always cheaper regardless of arrival pattern
Polling jobs cannot read from S3 under any circumstances
questions.explain: An event-driven trigger fires exactly when new data lands, avoiding wasted polling checks and matching cost/execution to actual arrival — ideal when arrival timing is unpredictable.
